Body: same issue : https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/49014

## Analysis of the attached debug bundle (`opencode-debug-20260926T001640.zip`)

I went through the logs from the debug export and sharing the findings in case they help triage.

### The freeze is renderer-side, not backend/service-side

- `main.log` is clean in every session: startup, v2 CLI/service startup, and the V1→V2 data migration all complete normally.
- `server-1/opencode.log` (~62k lines) shows nothing at the freeze timestamps; its only ERROR entries are from June and unrelated (aborted runs).
- Every freeze is recorded in `window.log` as `renderer unresponsive` for the main window.

### The unresponsive events fire exactly when a session is opened

In 5 of the 14 captured sessions, `window.log` logged `renderer unresponsive` — each one ~20 s after app start, i.e. right when the first session was opened (times below are local):

| Session dir | `app starting` (main.log) | first `renderer unresponsive` (window.log) |
|---|---|---|
| 20260925T235418 | 07:54:18 | 07:54:39 |
| 20260926T001134 | 08:11:34 | 08:11:54 |
| 20260926T001612 | 08:16:13 | 08:16:40 |

### Sampled stacks all land in the message list's stick-to-bottom virtualizer path

The `renderer unresponsive samples` captured by the main process always point at the same code path — a virtualized list (looks like TanStack Virtual) performing `scrollToEnd` on mount/measurement:

```
at Array.Re (oc://renderer/assets/main-C8RBRwI4.js:2:12238)
at Object.active (oc://renderer/assets/route-CHhjG5_X.js:89:64925)
at n (oc://renderer/assets/route-CHhjG5_X.js:89:51650)
at Object.scrollToFn (oc://renderer/assets/route-CHhjG5_X.js:89:53808)
at Ba._scrollToOffset (oc://renderer/assets/route-CHhjG5_X.js:2:44160)
at Ba.scrollToIndex (oc://renderer/assets/route-CHhjG5_X.js:2:42710)
at Ba.scrollToEnd (oc://renderer/assets/route-CHhjG5_X.js:2:43143)
```

Other samples enter the same class from different entry points: `Ba.scheduleScrollReconcile`, `Ba.getOffsetForIndex`, `P.resizeItem`. Bundle hashes differ between builds (`route-CDROkuzn.js`, `route-D7t6Qi_B.js`, `route-CHhjG5_X.js`) but the offsets are identical, so it is the same code across 2.0.x.

### renderer.log shows a ResizeObserver storm

Sessions that froze show bursts of `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications`, up to 248 lines in a single session:

- 20260925T235000: 248
- 20260925T235534: 205
- 20260925T152241: 74

One possibly relevant detail: renderer.log starts with `Slow network is detected. … Fallback font will be used while loading: oc://renderer/assets/Inter.ttf`. If the webfont swaps in after the list has already measured and scrolled, item heights change post-measurement — exactly the kind of event that would kick off a measure → scroll → measure loop.

### How this explains the reported symptoms

- **Freeze on session open**: the list mounts and sticks to the bottom; item heights change (late font swap, code blocks/diffs/images) → ResizeObserver re-measures → scrolls again → the loop pegs the renderer main thread at 100%.
- **Randomness**: whether the loop converges depends on font-load timing, item height variance, and window size — so the same session sometimes opens fine.
- **Title bar stays clickable**: the native caption buttons are handled by the OS, not by the frozen renderer.

### Relation to existing issues

This looks like the same family as #33712, #34289, #34038, #37997, #38296, #43355, #48633. One difference that may be useful for triage: in my captures the sampled stacks sit in the **session message list virtualizer (`scrollToEnd` stick-to-bottom)**, not in the composer-region observers analyzed in #33712. Also note PR #44883 only suppresses the ResizeObserver log noise — the freeze itself still reproduces on 2.0.18.

Happy to provide additional logs if needed.

Confirming this still reproduces on **2.0.18** (not fixed since 2.0.12), with a narrower trigger.

On 2.0.18 the V2 `permissions:` list works when the frontmatter contains only recognized keys, but **any unrecognized top-level key** routes the *entire* frontmatter — including `permissions` — into `request.body`, so nothing is applied. The common real-world trigger is the legacy `name:` field.

Minimal repro (two agents differing only by `name:`):

`~/.config/opencode/agents/_fresh_named.md`

```md
---
name: _fresh_named
description: repro with legacy name key
mode: subagent
permissions:
  - action: edit
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
  - action: shell
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
---
body
```

`~/.config/opencode/agents/_fresh_unnamed.md` — identical minus the `name:` line.

`opencode reload` then `opencode debug agents`:

```
_fresh_named     top-level permissions=[]                       request.body={'permissions': [edit deny, shell deny]}
_fresh_unnamed   top-level permissions=[edit deny, shell deny]  request.body={}
```

So on 2.0.18 the deny rules apply only for the file without `name:`.

Additional observations:

- It is not specific to `name`. Any unknown key behaves the same: with `unknownkey: hello` plus `permissions`, `request.body` contains both `unknownkey` and `permissions`, and the rules are still dropped.
- The legacy V1 block still works even with `name:` present (`permission: { edit: deny, bash: deny }` is applied as `shell`), so only the native V2 `permissions` key is affected.
- The migration guide lists agent `name` as accepted-but-unsupported and says it is ignored "with a warning"; no warning is emitted and `permissions` is silently discarded.
- Impact: a subagent intended to be read-only silently keeps default allow-all.
- Workaround while migrating: strip legacy/unrecognized frontmatter keys (especially `name`) so only recognized keys remain.

Large-N field data from a real release session: the missing stall bound is hit in ~0.9% of turns, and manual interruption is the only thing that ends them.

## Environment

- OpenCode: `2.0.18` (`latest` channel), Linux x64
- Client: TUI inside a terminal multiplexer, local service
- Providers/models: **11 distinct models** — `opencode-go` (`mimo-v2.6-flash`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `space-bunny-free`, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`), `opencode` (`deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `space-bunny-free`), `openai` (`gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna-fast`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-sol-fast`, `gpt-5.6-terra`)
- Plugins: one local `plan-auto-build` hook (no provider/stream involvement)
- `chunkTimeout` / `timeout`: **not set** in config — I read the issue as "these settings are silently ignored", so to be precise: this is not a repro of the config key failing, it is evidence that *no* client-side stall bound exists by default either.

## Data

Counted from `session_message` rows in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, over all assistant turns with a `time.completed`:

| | |
|---|---|
| assistant turns | **5,302** |
| turns where `time.streamed` is **null** (not one token emitted) | **47 (0.89%)** |
| of those, terminated only because the user interrupted | **43 / 47 (91%)** |
| mean duration of a never-streamed turn | **97.3 s** |
| worst | **830 s (13m50s)** |
| distinct models affected | **11** |

These are turns where the request was accepted and `time.created` was written, but no `streamed` timestamp ever arrived. They sit there until an interrupt is sent. Only 4 of the 47 ever ended on their own (network/TCP path); the other 43 waited for a human, including one that ran to 830s — far past the ~70s keepalive bound described above.

Because this spans 11 models across 3 providers, it does not look model- or provider-specific — consistent with the defect being in the shared `packages/llm` stream path rather than in any one upstream.

## Same-session A/B from today

Two consecutive windows in one session, same codebase, same machine, only the model changed:

```
model                   turns   never-streamed   mean TTFT   worst hang
mimo-v2.6-flash             11                2      29.8s        273s
deepseek-v4.1-flash          5                0      17.2s          —
```

On how this compares with #47951 and #48194:

#40149 converts the path at the `read`, `write`, `edit` and `apply_patch` permission requests. Project paths stay relative, and paths outside the worktree (or in a project with no git repo) reach the matcher as absolute paths, so the evaluator itself doesn't change.

#48194 does it in the matcher instead, which also covers other callers. It only tries the absolute candidate against rules starting with `/`, so Windows drive-letter rules miss it, and a deny on either candidate wins, which can change the result for configs that mix absolute and relative rules.

#47951 fixes a different problem: it resolves Windows junctions and symlinks in configured absolute patterns, and would work alongside either.

I'd take one of #40149 or #48194 rather than both, and keep #47951 either way. Thanks to both authors.

Narrowing the mechanism further, now that I have read the keymap defaults — this makes the defect sharper than my first analysis and changes which fix shape is smallest.

**`Enter` is bound to two commands.** On `dev` (`packages/tui/src/config/keybind.ts`):
- `:217` `"prompt.autocomplete.select": keybind("return", …)`
- `:163` `input_submit: keybind("return", "Submit input")`

The autocomplete registers its bindings with `enabled: () => Boolean(store.visible)` (`autocomplete.tsx:583`) on the input, so **while the slash list is open, `Enter` means "select", and submit never sees the key**. That is why file commands need two Enters and why the first one cannot submit: it is not a timing or render problem, the key is routed elsewhere.

**And the "cursor advances one space" is literally a text wipe plus rewrite.** `select()` (`:553-558`) runs `hide()` *before* `onSelect()`, and `hide()` (`:650-660`) clears the input when the text starts with `/` and has no trailing space:

```
props.input().deleteRange(0, 0, cursor.row, cursor.col)
```

So for `/good`: `hide()` deletes the whole typed command, then the file-command branch of `onSelect` (`:456-462`) inserts `"/good "` back. The command text reappears with a **trailing space** and the cursor at the end of it — exactly the one-position shift reported. Nothing was submitted, and the trailing space is also why the autocomplete does not reopen on the next keystroke (the `onInput` guard at `:682` sees whitespace before the cursor).

**Why built-ins differ:** same `Enter`, same `hide()`, but the built-in branch resolves to `keymap.dispatchCommand(entry.command.name)` (`keymap.tsx:286`) — an execution, not a rewrite — so it completes its action on the first press.

**Smallest fix shapes, in order of preference:**
1. Stop the autocomplete from staying open on an already-complete command name. `onInput` (`:676-700`) currently only hides on the two-token rule at `:684`; a bare `/good` stays open. Hiding when the input is a single token that matches a command hands the next `Enter` straight to `input_submit` — no prop threading, one predicate.
2. Thread a submit callback from the prompt into `Autocomplete` and have `select()` submit on an exact match (`Autocomplete` has no such prop today, `:75-86`).
3. Handle it inside the `prompt.autocomplete.select` run handler — least invasive to the completion path, but it puts submit semantics in a keymap handler rather than the component that owns the state.

I still want to work on this and will take shape 1 unless you prefer otherwise. Note there is currently **no autocomplete unit test** — `packages/tui/test/` has `prompt/` and `cli/tui/prompt-submit-race.test.ts` but nothing over the completion path — so the PR would add the first one, covering "exact match submits on one Enter" and "partial match still completes".

## Additional evidence: same defect on a built-in capability alias, macOS/arm64

This is not specific to third-party plugin tools. It reproduces for a **built-in** capability registered through `ctx.tool.transform` → `editor.add({ name })`, and the consequence is worse than a failed call: **hooks never see the failure.**

### Minimal reproduction

```js
export default {
  id: "agent-hygiene",
  async setup(ctx) {
    await ctx.tool.transform((editor) => {
      editor.add({ name: "bash", description: "Alias for the `shell` tool.", /* ... */ })
    })
  },
}
```

The host already exposes this capability natively as **`shell`**. After the plugin registers `bash`:

- the model-facing catalog advertises **`tools.bash`**,
- a direct `bash({ command })` call fails with `No tool named "bash" is currently available. Please use a tool from the available tool list.`,
- `tools.bash({ command })` inside a `{code}` block **succeeds** — the plugin's `execute` runs normally.

So the alias is reachable only through the code-execution path, exactly as described here.

### Why this is worse than a 404

Name resolution fails **before** `tool.execute.before` is dispatched. A guard that wants to observe or rewrite the call never runs, and there is no log line — a hook keyed on `event.tool` looks installed while silently never firing.

Measured over a 48h window on this host: **321 calls** failed with `No tool named "bash"`. Splitting at the plugin commit: **273 before, 44 after.** `editor.add({ name: "bash" })` did not put `bash` on the native tool list.

The existing harness lesson generalises from this: **match hooks on input shape** (`typeof event.input?.command === "string"`), never on a tool-name string. `shell`, `bash`, and `tools["ns"]["tool"]` are one capability with three surface names, and `event.tool` is the id of whichever surface happened to dispatch.

### Suggested fix directions

1. Register `ctx.tool.transform` additions on the **native** tool list, not only the catalog-visible one — so `bash(...)` resolves directly.
2. Or accept bare `bash` as an alias for `shell` at name resolution, so existing plugin aliases and the documented `bash` spelling both work.
3. Either way, consider surfacing "a plugin registered this name, reachable only via the code-execution path" rather than a generic "use a tool from the available tool list", which sends the model hunting the catalog.

### Environment

opencode v2 (binary), macOS 15 (darwin/arm64), global plugin at `~/.config/opencode/plugins/agent-hygiene/index.js`, hot-reloaded and confirmed active.
